subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the derivative of log x from the first principle with respect to x.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say how you combine the two logarithms and which standard limit finishes it.

steps.label: State the first principle
steps.margin_note: First mark. log here is the natural logarithm to base e. The domain is x > 0, so x + h stays positive for small h.
lines: Let f(x) = log x, x > 0  (logarithm to base e)

recall.must_convey: That the first principle is written with f(x) = log x, the natural logarithm, on x > 0.
accept: write the first principle with f of x equal to log x
take the limit of log x plus h minus log x over h
log means natural log to base e and x is positive
first principle rasta, log x plus h minus log x by h
start from the definition of the derivative

steps.why: The definition is the marked move, and naming the base matters: the answer 1/x is the natural logarithm result, not the base-10 one.
common_mistakes: Writing log(x + h) as log x + log h.
Quoting 1/x from the standard table with no limit work.
steps.memory_tip: Definition first. log(x + h) is the logarithm of the whole of x + h.

steps.label: Write it as one logarithm
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Dividing inside the logarithm gives the 1 + h/x form the standard limit needs. Note that (x + h)/x is 1 + h/x, not h/x.
lines: log A − log B = log(A/B), so
log(x + h) − log x = log((x + h)/x)

recall.must_convey: That log A − log B = log(A/B) is used, giving log(1 + h/x).
accept: log minus log is log of the quotient
log of x plus h by x is log of one plus h by x
combine the two logarithms into a single logarithm
log minus log ni log of quotient ga rasta
the argument becomes one plus h by x

steps.why: Two logarithms subtract into one, and the argument becomes 1 plus a small quantity — the exact shape the standard logarithm limit needs.
common_mistakes: Writing log(x + h) − log x as log(x + h)/log x.
Simplifying (x + h)/x to h/x and losing the 1.
steps.memory_tip: log minus log is log of the quotient. Here that quotient is 1 + h/x.

steps.label: Match the standard limit
steps.margin_note: Third mark. The standard limit is log(1 + t)/t → 1, so the denominator must be t and not h. The substitution h = xt is what supplies the 1/x.
lines: Put t = h/x. As h → 0, t → 0, and h = xt

recall.must_convey: That h/x is renamed t, h becomes xt, and the standard limit log(1 + t)/t = 1 is named.
accept: put t equal to h by x so the denominator becomes t
the standard limit is log of one plus t by t equals one
h becomes x t so one by x comes outside
t ni h by x ga substitute cheste one by x bayata vasthundi
match the denominator to the quantity added to one
heard_as: log one plus t by t
t equal to h by x

steps.why: The standard limit holds only when the denominator equals the quantity added to 1. Renaming h/x as t makes that true and leaves 1/x outside the limit.
common_mistakes: Using lim (log(1 + h/x))/h = 1, which is 1/x, not 1.
Renaming the argument but forgetting that h itself becomes xt.
steps.memory_tip: The standard limit needs the same small quantity above and below: log(1 + t) over t.

steps.label: Take the limit
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The 1/x came from the substitution, not from the limit — the limit itself contributes only 1. Keep the domain x > 0 beside the answer.

recall.must_convey: That the standard limit is 1, so the derivative is 1/x for x > 0.
accept: the answer is one by x
the limit is one so what is left is one by x
derivative of log x is one by x for positive x
one by x answer vasthundi
the standard limit contributes one and the one by x stays

steps.why: Every factor is now accounted for: the 1/x is outside the limit and the limit is 1, so nothing is left to evaluate.
common_mistakes: Giving 1/(x + h) by taking the limit in only part of the expression.
Giving (log x)/x by cancelling the wrong thing.
steps.memory_tip: The 1/x is the factor pulled outside; the logarithm limit contributes only 1.

insider_note: Combine the two logarithms into log(1 + h/x) before taking the limit. Then log(1 + t)/t → 1 with t = h/x, and the 1/x left outside is the answer.
